sub: Everything in place before the carrier door opens — tick it off as you go

cards.title: Buy Before They Arrive
checks: Litter boxes — one per cat, plus one
22–24 in interior. A storage tote works and is usually bigger.
Unscented fine clumping litter
Buy whatever the shelter used first, change gradually later.
A cat tree with a perch above 4 ft
Wide base, 14 in platforms, sisal posts.
Scratching post, 32 in or taller
Tall enough for a full stretch, rigid enough not to rock.
Wide shallow bowls, ceramic or steel
Never plastic — it scratches and causes chin acne.
A top-opening hard carrier
You lower a frightened cat in, rather than posting it through a hole.
Grooming brush for the coat type
Rubber pin brush for short, a comb for long.
A wand toy
The only toy that produces a real hunting sequence.

cards.title: Set Up The Safe Room
checks: Pick one quiet room
A spare bedroom or office. A bathroom works.
Box at one end, food and water at the other
Cats will not eliminate near where they eat.
A hiding place at floor level
A box on its side is enough.
A perch above it
Height is how a nervous cat feels safe.
Close the windows, check the screens
Cats survive falls that should kill them, then arrive with chest injuries.
Remove every lily from the house
Pollen alone causes acute kidney failure.
Tape down or box up loose cables
Have the vet's number and out-of-hours cover written down

cards.title: The First Week
checks: Day 1 — open the carrier and walk away
Do not lift the cat out. Most come out within an hour of being left alone.
Days 1–5 — expect hiding
Normal, not a problem. Keep feeding and scooping on schedule.
Twice a day — sit in the room and ignore the cat
Read aloud, work. Let it approach you. A slow blink is the one gesture worth offering.
When it eats in front of you — start wand play
Usually the moment things turn.
Then — open the house one room at a time
Keep the safe room available for several weeks.
Resident cat? Do not skip the scent stage
Swap bedding, then feed either side of a closed door, then brief visual contact.

cards.title: Ask The Shelter
checks: Is this cat good with dogs, children, other cats?
They have watched it. This is worth more than a pedigree.
What litter and food is it using now?
Change both gradually, not on day one.
Is it spayed or neutered, chipped, vaccinated?
Has it been FIV and FeLV tested?
Any known medical history or medication?
If a kitten — how old exactly?
Under 8 weeks is too young. Walk away, even if it is the one you want.

rules_post: People Get Wrong In The First Month
rules: A cat given the run of a house on day one has nowhere it understands, and hides under a bed for three weeks.
Pulling the cat out to reassure it.
Being reached for is the thing it is afraid of. Sitting nearby and ignoring it works faster.
One litter box, because two looks like a lot.
It is the leading behavioral reason cats end up back at the shelter.
It teaches the cat to scratch when you are not in the room, and damages the trust you need for everything else.
Assuming a hiding cat is unhappy.
Two to five days of hiding is a normal arrival. Not eating for 24 hours is not — that one is a vet call.
